solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Country girl in working group

indicators.note: the girl's name sits inside the group, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a bee is a gathering of people working together, as in a sewing bee
a short form of Elizabeth

explanation.surface: A girl from abroad is part of a team at work.
explanation.walkthrough: A bee is a gathering for shared work, as in a sewing bee or quilting bee.
explanation.definitionFit: Belize is a small nation in Central America on the Caribbean coast.

clue.text: Giant insects biting horse

indicators.note: the insects bite into the animal's letter, so it ends up held between them

blocks.note: the first insect
H is slang for heroin, which is also called horse
the second insect

explanation.surface: Swarming insects attack a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: Horse and H are both slang for heroin, which links the two. The plural insects supplies two different ones.
explanation.definitionFit: A behemoth is a huge creature, from the biblical beast, so anything giant.

clue.text: Article in El País about copper's whereabouts

indicators.note: about means around, so the article wraps the metal

blocks.note: los is a Spanish definite article, and El País is a Spanish newspaper
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A Spanish newspaper runs a story about a policeman's location.
explanation.definitionFit: A locus is a particular position or place, which is what whereabouts means.

clue.text: Philosophy getting up Jean-Paul Sartre's nose?

indicators.note: in a down entry getting up means rising, so the word is read from the bottom

blocks.note: nez is French for nose, and Sartre was French

explanation.surface: Eastern philosophy annoys the French existentialist.
explanation.walkthrough: Getting up someone's nose is British slang for irritating them.
explanation.definitionFit: Zen is a school of Buddhism, a philosophy stressing meditation.

clue.text: Comic introducing a man of the cloth

indicators.note: introducing a letter means putting it into the comedian's name

blocks.note: Charlie Chaplin, the silent-film comedian
taken as written

explanation.surface: A comedian brings on a clergyman as his straight man.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaplain is a clergyman attached to an institution such as a regiment, prison or college.

clue.text: Nothing in plea for protection making one fearful

indicators.note: in places the zero inside the plea

blocks.note: hide us! is a cry for shelter
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A frightened person begs to be sheltered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fearful' looks like scared, but here means dreadful to look at.
explanation.definitionFit: Fearful can mean frightful or dreadful, and hideous is something dreadfully ugly.

clue.text: One who dines selectively, chopping up certain apes

indicators.note: chopping something up cuts it into bits that can be rearranged

blocks.note: all eleven letters are the fodder

explanation.surface: A fussy eater chops up some apes, a grisly picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A pescetarian eats fish but no meat, choosing their food with care.

clue.text: Sketch outline of a dozy judge

blocks.note: taken as written
dozy means stupid, dumb
to rate something is to judge it

explanation.surface: An artist draws a rough picture of a sleepy judge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Judge' is a verb, not a person in a wig.
explanation.definitionFit: To adumbrate is to give a faint or partial indication of something, a sketchy outline.

clue.text: One must stop impossible impulse

indicators.note: to stop something is to plug it, so the one goes into the gap

blocks.note: not on is British slang for out of the question
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone must resist an impossible urge.
explanation.definitionFit: A notion can be a sudden whim or inclination, an impulse to do something.

clue.text: Sign of unity among neo-Marxists for example

definitions.text: Sign of unity among neo-Marxists for example

blocks.note: surface reading: a symbol of solidarity within a left-wing faction
setter's reading: the punctuation mark joining neo to Marxists in the clue itself

explanation.surface: Neo-Marxists display an emblem of their solidarity.
explanation.walkthrough: No hidden run of letters here: the sign is punctuation, and neo-Marxists is the example printed in front of you.
explanation.definitionFit: The short dash joins two words into one compound, so it literally signals unity between them.

clue.text: Worn out husband covered in spots, might one say?

indicators.note: what one might say is spoken, so the phrase is matched by its sound rather than its spelling

blocks.note: H is the standard abbreviation for husband
someone covered in spots has acne, so might be called acne'd

explanation.surface: A spotty, exhausted husband describes his appearance.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke word acne'd, meaning afflicted with spots, is said like the back of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Hackneyed means stale or overused, so a worn-out phrase is a hackneyed one.

clue.text: After change of heart I'm not going to move

indicators.note: the heart is the central letter, and it is swapped for a different one

blocks.note: shan't is a flat refusal, short for shall not

explanation.surface: Someone who has had a change of heart now refuses to budge.
explanation.walkthrough: SHAN'T has its middle letter A changed to U, giving SHUNT.
explanation.definitionFit: To shunt is to push or shift something aside, as railway wagons are shunted onto a siding.

clue.text: Shipmate Ron sadly becoming a loner potentially?

indicators.note: something gone sadly wrong is in a mess, so the letters are disordered

blocks.note: all eleven letters are the fodder

explanation.surface: A sailor called Ron is sadly turning into a solitary figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A misanthrope dislikes other people and so may well keep away from them, hence a potential loner.

clue.text: On we ran desperate, now to take shelter far away

indicators.note: desperate means frantic and wild, so these letters are thrown into disorder
something taking shelter goes inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: seven letters of fodder
here can mean now, at this point

explanation.surface: A desperate group runs on, looking for somewhere to shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: The shuffled letters split into two words so the third can shelter between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Nowhere near means a long way off, a phrase for far away.

clue.text: Rounds on bishop? I don't think much of that

definitions.text: I don't think much of that

indicators.note: in a across entry one thing placed on another follows it, so the two pieces join in order

blocks.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
two round letters O

explanation.surface: Someone scorns a bishop's rounds of visits.
explanation.walkthrough: Rounds are O-shapes, so two Os; they go on (after) B.
explanation.definitionFit: Boo is the noise of disapproval a crowd makes, just what one says when unimpressed.

clue.text: Add a way to restart play

blocks.note: first meaning: to include something extra, as a verb phrase
second meaning: in football, the ball is returned from the touchline by hand

explanation.walkthrough: The verb phrase throw in and the noun throw-in share their letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Throwing in a bonus means including it, and a throw-in is how football resumes after the ball leaves the pitch at the side.

clue.text: President's sole veto altered by Republican

indicators.note: altered means changed, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: eight letters of fodder
R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: A Republican overturns a president's only veto.
explanation.walkthrough: The R is added before the shuffle, so all nine letters are mixed.
explanation.definitionFit: Theodore and Franklin D. Roosevelt were both Presidents of the United States.

clue.text: Reportedly understand how to make main course?

indicators.note: what is reported is passed on by word of mouth, so sound matters, not spelling

blocks.note: to see is to understand and a way is how something is done

explanation.surface: A cookery question: grasp the method for preparing the principal dish.
explanation.walkthrough: The main is the sea, as in the Spanish Main, so a main course is a route across it.
explanation.definitionFit: A seaway is a shipping route or channel over the open sea, a course through the main.

clue.text: Plump for jam pudding

blocks.note: first meaning: round and chubby
second meaning: a British suet pudding rolled up with jam and baked or steamed

explanation.walkthrough: 'Plump for' reads as choose; plump is the adjective and for only joins. A roly-poly is a British suet pudding spread with jam and rolled up.
explanation.definitionFit: Roly-poly describes a chubby figure, and jam roly-poly is a classic British school dessert.

clue.text: Enemy close by, Spooner says. I don't think so!

indicators.note: Rev. Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of neighbouring words

blocks.note: a foe is an enemy; it gives up its F sound and takes the N
near means close by; it takes the F sound in exchange

explanation.surface: Warned the enemy is near, someone dismisses the danger.
explanation.definitionFit: No fear is a British colloquial refusal, meaning certainly not or not likely.

clue.text: Brazilian diplomacy? It might quell disorder

blocks.note: Rio de Janeiro, the Brazilian city
tact is diplomacy

explanation.surface: Brazil's diplomacy may calm unrest.
explanation.walkthrough: The Riot Act was a British law of 1714; reading it ordered a crowd to disperse.
explanation.definitionFit: The Riot Act was read to a rowdy crowd to make it disperse, so it quelled disorder.

clue.text: Resign from oil giant, ignoring son? Exactly

indicators.note: ignoring something means leaving it out, so a letter is dropped

blocks.note: to quit a job is to resign from it
Esso is the brand of the oil company ExxonMobil
S is the standard abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Someone quits a big oil company, without their son.
explanation.walkthrough: One S is taken from ESSO, a familiar petrol brand in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Quite so is a formal phrase of agreement, saying the same as exactly.

clue.text: Case of Eros making you shudder?

blocks.note: first meaning: the holder for Cupid's arrows
second meaning: to tremble

explanation.walkthrough: 'Case of' suggests a legal case or a first letter; it is a container for arrows.
explanation.definitionFit: Eros, the love god, carries arrows in a sheath, and to tremble with emotion is also the same word.

clue.text: Artistic performer given her head?

blocks.note: surface reading: a performer allowed free rein to do as she likes
setter's reading: the biblical dancer handed John the Baptist's head on a platter

explanation.walkthrough: Given her head is an idiom for being allowed free rein; here it is meant literally.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible and in Strauss's opera the dancing princess asks for and receives the Baptist's severed head.

clue.text: A lover once coming back in chopper

indicators.note: coming back means travelling the other way, so the former partner is read backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
an ex is a former partner

explanation.surface: A former lover returns by helicopter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chopper' suggests a helicopter, but here it is a tool for chopping.
explanation.definitionFit: An axe is a tool for chopping wood, and chopper is a slang word for one.

clue.text: Key partner welcoming proposal in excited manner

indicators.note: to welcome someone is to take them in, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: E is a musical key
a motion is a proposal put to a meeting
an ally is a partner

explanation.surface: An important partner responds enthusiastically to a marriage proposal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key partner' reads as one phrase but is two pieces, the key and the partner, which wrap round the proposal.
explanation.definitionFit: To act emotionally is to act with strong feeling, which is an excited manner.

clue.text: Monk astride large beast of burden

indicators.note: astride means with legs on either side, so one piece straddles the other

blocks.note: a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist monk
L is the abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A monk rides a large pack animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Llamas are South American animals used to carry loads in the Andes.

clue.text: Fat old cow's complaint about ending of lease

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its final letter
about means surrounding, so the disease wraps round the single letter

blocks.note: O is the standard abbreviation for old
BSE, mad cow disease
the last letter of lease

explanation.surface: An old cow grumbles about the terms of her tenancy ending.
explanation.walkthrough: BSE (bovine spongiform encephalopathy) goes round E; O goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Obese means very overweight, a stronger synonym for fat.

clue.text: A coffee with remarkably nice aroma

indicators.note: something remarkable is out of the ordinary, so the letters fall into an unusual order

blocks.note: all nine letters are the fodder

explanation.surface: A cup of coffee that smells remarkably good.
explanation.definitionFit: An Americano is a coffee made by adding hot water to espresso.

clue.text: Unmarried philosopher not himself

indicators.note: unmarried means without the married mark, so that letter is dropped

blocks.note: John Stuart Mill, the philosopher

explanation.surface: A bachelor philosopher is out of sorts.
explanation.walkthrough: M is the abbreviation for married, removed from MILL.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone not himself is unwell or off colour, which is what ill means.

clue.text: Whole of body holding on

indicators.note: a thing holding another has it inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: an entity is a body, as in a legal or corporate body
re means on or concerning

explanation.surface: The whole of one's body keeps hanging on.
explanation.definitionFit: The entirety of something is all of it, the whole.

clue.text: Times in which king is tired?

indicators.note: in which says the second piece sits inside the first

blocks.note: by is multiplication, as in three by four
King Lear of Shakespeare's play

explanation.surface: A sleepy period during which the monarch feels weary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like a period or the newspaper; it is the multiplication word BY.
explanation.definitionFit: Bleary eyes are dim from tiredness, so bleary describes someone tired.
